name: Nature
template_note: Nature accepts LaTeX (all text, references, tables and legends in one .tex file) and a single PDF up to 30 MB at first submission; it converts to Word after acceptance. There is no Nature-specific class to install.
notes: Summary paragraph: ideally no more than 200 words, fully referenced.
Title: at most 75 characters including spaces.
About 2,500 words for a 6-page Article, 4,300 for 8 pages.
Methods typically no more than 3,000 words, with separate Data and Code availability statements.
Typically no more than 50 references (Methods references not counted).
Double-spaced, line-numbered, 12-point Times New Roman.
Life-science Articles also need a Reporting Summary.

name: Nature Communications
template_note: Initial submissions are format-free; the editor sends formatting instructions at revision. Nature Portfolio reference style is used.
notes: Abstract: no more than 200 words and no references.
Title: at most 15 words.
Main text ideally at most 5,000 words; Methods typically under 3,000.
At most 70 references and up to 10 display items.
Discussion has no subheadings.

name: Science
template_note: Science prefers one .docx with figures and tables embedded. LaTeX users should convert to .docx, or use Science's own LaTeX template and upload a PDF. Materials and Methods go in the Supplementary Materials.
notes: Research Article: main text at most 3,000 words, 3 to 5 display items, about 50 main-text references.
Abstract: 125 words or less, no citations or abbreviations.
Title: at most 96 characters including spaces.
Single-spaced, US letter, Times New Roman.
Citations are italic numbers in parentheses, e.g. (18, 19); reference lists give every author (no et al.).
Figure captions: bold one-line title, at most 200 words.
Data underlying figures as Data S1, a multi-sheet Excel workbook.

name: Cell
template_note: Cell takes a single PDF or Word file at first submission. Cell Press offers an optional template; LaTeX is converted to Word for copyediting. STAR Methods formatting is finalised with the editor at acceptance.
notes: Under 7,000 words including main figure legends (STAR Methods, supplemental legends and references excluded); at most 7 figures and/or tables.
Summary of at most 150 words; 3-4 Highlights of at most 85 characters; eTOC blurb of at most 50 words.
Section order: Summary, Keywords, Introduction, Results, Limitations of the study, Discussion, Resource availability, then STAR Methods.
References are numbered (Cell style; up to 10 authors, then et al.).

name: The New England Journal of Medicine
template_note: NEJM wants one double-spaced file (preferably Word) with text, references, legends and tables. The Supplementary Appendix must be sent as both PDF and Word, paginated with a table of contents.
notes: Original Article: at most 2,700 words (introduction to discussion), at most 5 tables and figures, up to 40 references.
Abstract: at most 250 words in four labelled paragraphs (Background, Methods, Results, Conclusions), plus a trial registration number if any.
References double-spaced; six or fewer authors listed in full, seven or more as the first three and et al.
Submit the protocol and statistical analysis plan when applicable.

name: The Lancet
template_note: The Lancet has no LaTeX class; this follows its Information for Authors (Vancouver superscript citations after punctuation, mid-line decimal points, Research in context panel). Supplementary material goes in one PDF with a table of contents.
notes: Article: up to 3,500 words (4,500 for randomised trials) and 30 references.
Summary: at most 300 words in five paragraphs (Background, Methods, Findings, Interpretation, Funding), no references.
Research in context panel (Evidence before this study, Added value of this study, Implications of all the available evidence), no references.
Data sharing statement required at the end of the manuscript.
Seven or more authors: first three, then et al.

name: JAMA
template_note: JAMA takes the manuscript as a Word document only (no PDF), double-spaced in 10-12 point type with a ragged right margin. The PDF here is for your own review.
notes: Original Investigation: at most 3,000 words and 5 tables/figures.
Structured abstract of at most 350 words.
Key Points (Question, Findings, Meaning) of 75-100 words before the abstract.
AMA Manual of Style, 11th edition (references: first three authors and et al. when there are more than six).
Individual files ideally at most 1 MB; all files at most 5 MB.

name: Genes (MDPI)
template_note: MDPI publishes Word and LaTeX templates, but their terms forbid reposting them, so they are not bundled. MDPI accepts free-format first submissions that contain the required sections; LaTeX submissions are a ZIP of all sources and images.
notes: Structured abstract of about 250 words (Background/Objectives, Methods, Results, Conclusions).
3 to 10 keywords.
Citations in square brackets before punctuation, e.g. [1], [1-3].
Total submission at most 120 MB.

name: arXiv
template_note: Upload the arxiv/ folder as a .tar.gz or .zip: arXiv compiles main.tex itself with pdfLaTeX. The bibliography is inlined, so no .bbl or BibTeX run is needed. Data and code ride along as ancillary files in anc/.
notes: Single-spaced (arXiv asks authors not to submit in referee mode).
Figures are PDF/PNG/JPEG for pdfLaTeX.
No hidden files, no build outputs (.aux, .log, .pdf) in the upload.
